title: Network Components and Devices
objective: Study-guide review — CISSP — Domain 4: Communication and Network Security: Network Components and Devices.

items: Hub — Layer 1; broadcasts to all ports (no intelligence, obsolete)
Switch — Layer 2; forwards based on MAC address; creates collision domains
Router — Layer 3; forwards based on IP address; creates broadcast domains
Gateway — Connects different network architectures or protocols
Layer 3 Switch — Combines switching and routing capabilities

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: Switches operate at Layer 2 by default (using MAC addresses). Layer 3 switches can also route using IP addresses. Routers create broadcast domain boundaries — broadcast traffic does NOT cross a router.

items: Packet Filtering (Stateless) — Layer 3; examines individual packets; no context
Stateful Inspection — Layer 3-4; tracks connection state; allows related return traffic
Application Proxy — Layer 7; deep content inspection; breaks client-server connection
Next-Generation Firewall (NGFW) — Combines stateful, application awareness, and IPS
Web Application Firewall (WAF) — Protects web applications from Layer 7 attacks

blocks.text: From Stewart: "Static packet-filtering firewalls are known as first-generation firewalls; they operate at layer 3 (the Network layer). Application-level gateway firewalls are also called proxy firewalls."

From Chapple: "CBAC (Context-Based Access Control) is a feature of firewall software that intelligently filters TCP and UDP packets based on application layer protocol session information." ⚠️ Exam Trap: A proxy firewall BREAKS the client-server connection — the client connects to the proxy, and the proxy creates a NEW connection to the server. This provides the deepest inspection but is also the slowest.

items: IDS (Intrusion Detection System) — Monitors and ALERTS; passive
IPS (Intrusion Prevention System) — Monitors and BLOCKS; active (inline)
NIDS/NIPS — Network-based; monitors network traffic
HIDS/HIPS — Host-based; monitors system activity
Detection methods: Signature-based (known attacks) vs. Anomaly-based (behavioral)

rows: False positives may block legitimate traffic

items: Signature-based — Matches known attack patterns; fast; cannot detect zero-day attacks
Anomaly-based — Learns normal behavior; detects novel attacks; higher false positives
Heuristic — Uses rules and algorithms; balance between signature and anomaly

blocks.title: Exam trap
blocks.text: ⚠️ Exam Trap: IDS is PASSIVE (detect and alert). IPS is ACTIVE (detect and block). An IPS must be INLINE (in the traffic path) to block traffic.

items: Forward Proxy — Represents internal clients to external servers
Reverse Proxy — Represents external clients to internal servers
Provides anonymity, caching, content filtering, and logging
Application-level proxy provides deep packet inspection
Can enforce security policies on outbound traffic
Distributes traffic across multiple servers for availability
Round-robin, least connections, IP hash — common algorithms
Provides high availability and fault tolerance
Can perform SSL offloading (terminates SSL at the load balancer)
Improves both performance and resilience
